definition.name: NXroot
definition.doc:
The root of a NeXus file.
NXroot defines only NeXus groups of type NXentry; a file may still have other content groups and fields at its root, which no NeXus item describes and NeXus tools do not validate. NXroot defines NeXus attributes of the root group, which annotate the content tree.
Note that NXroot is the only base class that does not inherit from the NXobject class, since the latter defines NeXus items that are not allowed at the root level.

attribute.name: file_time
attribute.doc: Date and time file was originally created

attribute.name: file_name
attribute.doc: File name of original NeXus file

attribute.name: file_update_time
attribute.doc: Date and time of last file change at close

attribute.name: NeXus_version
attribute.doc:
Version of NeXus API used in writing the file.
Note that this is different from the version of the base class or application definition version number.

attribute.name: NeXus_repository
attribute.doc: A repository containing the application definitions used for creating this file. If the ``NeXus_release`` attribute contains a commit distance and hash, this should refer to this repository.

attribute.name: NeXus_release
attribute.doc:
The version of NeXus definitions used in writing the file. This can either be a date-based NeXus release (e.g., YYYY.MM), see https://github.com/nexusformat/definitions/releases or a version tag that includes additional development information, such as a commit distance and a Git hash. This is typically formatted as `vYYYY.MM.post1.dev<commit-distance>-g<git-hash>`, where `YYYY.MM` refers to the base version of the NeXus definitions. `post1.dev<commit-distance>` indicates that the definitions are based on a commit after the base version (post1), with `<commit-distance>` being the number of commits since that version. `g<git-hash>` is the abbreviated Git hash that identifies the specific commit of the definitions being used.
If the version includes both a commit distance and a Git hash, the ``NeXus_repository`` attribute must be included, specifying the URL of the repository containing that version.

attribute.name: HDF_version
attribute.doc: Version of HDF (version 4) library used in writing the file

attribute.name: HDF5_Version
attribute.doc:
Version of HDF5 library used in writing the file.
Note this attribute is spelled with uppercase "V", different than other version attributes.

attribute.name: XML_version
attribute.doc: Version of XML support library used in writing the XML file

attribute.name: h5py_version
attribute.doc: Version of h5py Python package used in writing the file

attribute.name: creator
attribute.doc: facility or program where file originated

attribute.name: creator_version
attribute.doc: Version of facility or program used in writing the file

attribute.name: NX_class
attribute.doc: Type of the root NeXus group: the name of its class.

attribute.name: default
attribute.doc:
.. index:: find the default plottable data .. index:: plotting .. index:: default attribute value
Declares which :ref:`NXentry` group contains the data to be shown by default. It is used to resolve ambiguity when more than one :ref:`NXentry` group exists. The value :ref:`names <validItemName>` the default :ref:`NXentry` group. The value must be the name of a child of the current group. The child must be a content group (which may be a content link).
It is recommended (as of NIAC2014) to use this attribute to help define the path to the default dataset to be plotted. See https://www.nexusformat.org/2014_How_to_find_default_data.html for a summary of the discussion.

fieldAttributes.doc:
NeXus attributes that any field directly in NXroot may have, whether or not NXroot defines that field.
A copy of the ``fieldAttributes`` of :ref:`NXobject`, which ``NXroot`` does not extend. Keep both the same.
A NeXus attribute of the NeXus field itself takes precedence over the one with the same name defined here.

attribute.name: target
attribute.doc:
Absolute path of the target of this content field, for example ``/entry/instrument/detector/data``.
When the value differs from the path of this content field, this content field is a content link to the content field at that path and has the same shared content (see :ref:`Design-Links`). The content field at that path is not a content link itself.

attribute.name: units
attribute.doc:
Units of the field values.
See :ref:`Design-Units`. When the NeXus field has a units category, such as ``NX_LENGTH``, the value of this NeXus attribute must be units of that category.

attribute.name: long_name
attribute.doc:
Descriptive name of the field (may include whitespace and engineering units).
Often used as the axis label on a plot.

attribute.name: interpretation
attribute.doc:
What the last dimensions of the field values are, so that plotting software can display them in a natural way.
For example, a 512 x 512 x 512 field with ``@interpretation`` set to ``spectrum`` is a 512 x 512 grid of spectra of 512 bins.

attribute.name: calibration_status
attribute.doc: Status of the field values.

attribute.name: stride
attribute.doc: Step between the stored values in each dimension, one value per dimension, when the values are not stored in C order (see :ref:`Design-NonCStorageOrder`). Used together with ``data_offset``.

attribute.name: data_offset
attribute.doc: Position of the first stored value in each dimension, one value per dimension, when the values are not stored in C order (see :ref:`Design-NonCStorageOrder`). Used together with ``stride``.

attribute.name: variant
attribute.doc: Name of the field in the same group that holds an earlier value of this field, for example ``beam_center_x_refined`` for ``beam_center_x`` (see :ref:`Design-Variants`).
